itens.descricao_en: The open-source Dynamic Island for React, installed with shadcn.
itens.readme:
# islandcn
A Dynamic Island-style component for any React app, installed with shadcn. Show an upload, a timer, a song, a ride on its way, an incoming call or a recording in one island at the top of your app, and shape each activity around your app's own actions.
```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://islandcn.dev/r/island-core.json
```
```tsx
"use client";
import { Island, IslandProvider, useIsland } from "@/lib/island";
// Mount once near the root.
 ;
// Then, from any component inside it:
const island = useIsland();
const upload = island.start({
  id: "upload",
  label: "Uploading report.pdf",
  compact: { leading:  , trailing:   },
  expanded: { center:  report.pdf , bottom:   },
});
upload.update({ compact: { trailing:   } });
upload.end();
```
## What's here
- **The engine** (`lib/island/`, registry item `island-core`): the activity stack, four presentations (idle, compact, the split, expanded), springs fitted to frame-by-frame recordings of the real island, long-press, alerts and reduced motion. React only.
- **Presets** (`components/islandcn/`): upload, timer, now playing, incoming call, ride or delivery ETA, recording, nearby transfer, battery and the split, each one file on the engine, plus the content kit they share.
- **The playground** (`/playground`): build an island for your app from a preset or a blank activity, fire every action, tune the motion and copy the install command and the code.
- **The site and docs** (`app/`, `docs/content/`).
Coding agents can use the optional `islandcn-skill` registry item as an install helper; see `/docs/agent-skill`.
## Develop
```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev           # http://localhost:3000
pnpm typecheck
pnpm build         # builds the registry into public/r, then the site
```
Read `AGENTS.md` before changing anything.
The recordings the motion was fitted to are not in this repo. `/lab` still plays every transition from its built-in sequences in `pnpm dev`; `/compare`, which sets the web side against the recordings, has nothing to show, and the one test that reads them is skipped.
## License
MIT, copyright (c) 2026 Leo. See `LICENSE`. islandcn copies the look and motion of Apple's island, but none of Apple's assets. It is not affiliated with Apple. Dynamic Island is a trademark of Apple Inc.

itens.readme:
# UI SDK
A library of behaviors for agents to build the next generation of user interfaces.
Keyboard navigation, focus, selection, dismissal, popups, drag and drop and the ARIA they need live in `@ui-sdk/core`, with adapters for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Components.
**[Read the docs](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs)**
## Install
UI SDK is in beta. Install core and the adapter for your framework:
```bash
npm install @ui-sdk/react @ui-sdk/core
```
For other frameworks, swap `@ui-sdk/react` for `@ui-sdk/vue`, `@ui-sdk/svelte`, `@ui-sdk/solid` or `@ui-sdk/web`.
Then give your agent the UI SDK skill:
```bash
npx skills add vercel-labs/ui --skill ui-sdk
```
## Example
Every component in UI SDK is built from behaviors. You start by creating the primitive with behaviors.
Don't worry, you don't need to learn how to write this. Your agents will. And we made them really good at it.
```ts
import { createFocusRecovery, definePrimitive } from "@ui-sdk/core"
const searchField = definePrimitive({
  name: "search-field",
  state: () => ({ value: "" }),
  api: (context) => ({
    set: (value: string) => context.store.set({ value }),
    recovery: createFocusRecovery({ fallback: () => context.element("input") }),
  }),
  slots: (slot) => ({
    input: slot({
      attrs: (state) => ({ value: state.value }),
      on: {
        input: (event, { api }) =>
          api.set((event.target as HTMLInputElement).value),
      },
    }),
    clear: slot({
      present: (state) => state.value !== "",
      attrs: () => ({ type: "button" }),
      press: ({ api }) => api.set(""),
      bind: (el, part) => part.api.recovery.bind(el, part),
    }),
  }),
})
export { searchField }
```
Then render it in your framework with `createParts`. The parts are the same in all five.
### React
```tsx
import { createParts } from "@ui-sdk/react/primitive"
import { searchField } from "./search-field"
const parts = createParts(searchField, { input: "input", clear: "button" })
const SearchField = parts.Root
const SearchFieldInput = parts.Input
const SearchFieldClear = parts.Clear

}
export { Search }
```

Sketch Material 3 Expressive screens in the browser, link them, tap through them, and copy a prompt for your AI coding tool. 
 Sketch the screens, tap through the flow, copy the prompt, and let your AI coding tool build the app. ( mp4 ) 
M3E Canvas is a free, open-source sketchpad for app screens made of real Material 3 Expressive parts. It runs entirely in your browser: no account, no server, nothing to install. What you sketch becomes a precise prompt that any AI coding tool that takes one, such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Cursor, can turn into a working app.
##   How it works
1. **Sketch** — Drag parts onto phone or desktop screens. They snap together and line up on a 4dp grid.
2. **Tap through** — Link parts to screens and press Preview to try the flow, transitions included.
3. **Copy the prompt** — The whole design becomes a short brief in your language. Paste it into your AI coding tool.
##   What's inside
  **Real M3 Expressive parts** — Buttons, FABs, bars, tabs, cards, lists, sheets, pickers, carousels, loading indicators and more, each with its own panel for text, style, size and what a tap does.
  **Screens and flow** — Phone and desktop screens, screens that scroll, taps and swipes that open other screens with the transition you pick, and arrows that show the whole flow.
  **Theme in one place** — Color, shape, type and motion: seven palettes or your own seed color, light and dark, three contrast levels, corner styles, fonts and the expressive spring motion.
  **Optional AI help** — Bring your own key to draft a design or write notes for you, or copy an instruction for a coding agent that replies with a share link. Keys never leave your browser.
  Everything it can do  
- **Parts** – buttons, icon buttons, FABs and extended FABs, FAB menus, split buttons, chips, top app bars, navigation bars and rails, floating toolbars, tabs, search bars, cards, list items, boxes, bottom sheets, dialogs, snackbars, text fields, dropdowns, switches, checkboxes, radio buttons, sliders, date and time pickers, text, images, carousels, camera and map placeholders, dividers, the shape-morphing loading indicator and wavy progress indicators. Every part has a panel for its text, style, size and alignment, and a trigger tab for what a tap does.

itens.descricao_en: A Claude Code skill that reverse-engineers any animation frame by frame, then proves the copy moves the same.
itens.readme:
reanimate 
  Reverse-engineer animations you like. Build your own on top.  A Claude Code skill that works from a live site, a screen recording, an mp4, a gif or a Lottie file. 
  A short demo.  Watch the full video .  
A lot of good ideas start on someone else's site. Ask an agent to rebuild one from a link or a screenshot and it makes one pass, calls it done, and misses. It can't see the motion or tell how far off it is.
reanimate records the original, rebuilds it in your code, then records the copy the same way and compares the two. Each round shows what's still off, so the agent keeps going until the numbers match. You end up with a close starting point to make your own.
  Three cards from stripe.com. Top: the original. Bottom: the copy, filmed the same way.  
## Install
```sh
npx skills add NiazMorshed2007/reanimate -g
```
The [skills CLI](https://skills.sh) asks which agents to set up; add `-a claude-code` to skip the question. Then, in Claude Code, say what you want, where it is and where it should go:
```text
/reanimate the hero entrance on https://example.com, into components/Hero.tsx
/reanimate this loader, 0:03 to 0:05 of ~/Downloads/loader.mov
/reanimate the card hover in this gif, match it exactly
/reanimate the logo marquee from https://example.com, with our logos and pause on hover
```
Needs [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.1 or later, on macOS or Linux (Windows is untested). The first run installs a static ffmpeg into the skill's folder and Playwright's Chromium into Playwright's usual cache, about 250 MB together. No API keys. Other agents that read `SKILL.md` can install it too, but it has only been tested with Claude Code.
## How it works
1. **Record.** It films the reference in a headless browser at a fixed viewport and frame rate: a video, numbered frames, every CSS and Web Animations API animation it finds, and the position of chosen elements on every frame. For canvas and WebGL it also traces the GPU calls (shaders, uniforms, draw calls, the three.js scene) on a virtual clock that makes every capture identical.
2. **Spec.** One row per element per property: start, duration, from → to, easing, stagger. A row with a "?" means the frames haven't been read yet.
3. **Build.** It writes the animation with what your project already uses: CSS, Framer Motion, GSAP, three.js.
4. **Verify.** It films the copy the same way, compares timing, easing and pixels, and makes side-by-side sheets.
5. **Repeat.** It fixes the biggest difference and films again, us

# hairline
Thirty-three isometric line figures that answer the pointer. For React and for anything with a DOM.
[ ](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lucasmarkes/hairline)
[ ](https://github.com/lucasmarkes/hairline/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[ ](./LICENSE)
Live, with a slider for `intensity`: **[hairline.lucasmarkes.com](https://hairline.lucasmarkes.com)**
  Featured sponsors   Your logo here  
## Install
```sh
npm i @lucasmarkes/hairline
```
No dependencies. ESM only. React 18 or later is an optional peer, needed only by `@lucasmarkes/hairline/react`.
With shadcn, which adds the package and a wrapper that reads your theme's tokens:
```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://hairline.lucasmarkes.com/r/hairline.json
```
## Use
### React
```tsx
import { Terrain } from "@lucasmarkes/hairline/react";
export function Hero() {
  return  ;
}
```
The figure fills its parent's width at a 5:4 aspect ratio. The entry is a client module, so a Server Component can render it with no `"use client"` of its own. Every component takes the options below and every ` ` attribute, and forwards its ref to the ` `.
### Anything else
```ts
import { terrain } from "@lucasmarkes/hairline";
const figure = terrain(document.getElementById("figure")!, { play: true });
figure.update({ intensity: 0.8 });
figure.destroy();
```
A figure draws into the element you give it, at the element's width and a 5:4 aspect ratio. `update` changes options on the running figure; `destroy` removes what the figure added. That is the shape of a Svelte action, so `use:terrain={{ intensity }}` works as it is.
## The figures
| Function | Component | What it is | A stronger `intensity` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `riffle` | `Riffle` | A tray of eight cards. The card under the pointer stands up; the arrow keys walk the cards. | The ripple spreads further from the pulled card. |
| `terrain` | `Terrain` | Eighty-one pillars on a plinth that rise around the pointer. | A wider area rises. |
| `exploded` | `Exploded` | An app window in four layers. Moving across opens the gap; moving down picks a layer. | The layers open further. |
| `phosphor` | `Phosphor` | A dot matrix that plays a loop, and fades like phosphor where the pointer paints it. | The trail lingers longer. |
| `slow` | `Slow` | Crates riding a belt through a gate. Hovering slows the clock without stopping it. | Time slows down more. |

### The Declarative JSON Gantt Chart Engine
**Where human intuition meets declarative AI planning.**
[ ](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

Turn any declarative JSON document into a high-performance, interactive, draggable Gantt chart.  
**Zero runtime dependencies.** **100% pure TypeScript.**  
Runs everywhere: Plain HTML, React, Next.js, Node.js CLI, and autonomous AI toolchains.
Designed from the ground up for:
* **Autonomous AI Agents & LLMs** - Declarative JSON schema contract eliminates UI hallucinations; models generate timeline data with 10x fewer tokens than fragile JSX code.
* **Students, Hobbyists & Creators** - Lightweight, beautiful Swiss Noir dark mode, intuitive drag-and-drop, touch gestures, and instant local storage persistence.
* **Engineering Teams & Program Directors** - Operations Research Critical Path solver, EVM (Earned Value Management), DCMA-14 schedule health audits, and multi-user CRDT collaboration with secure role-based permissions.
[Live Playground](https://ahmadhassan-bted.github.io/Jantt/) • [JSON Cheatsheet](./docs/JANTT_JSON_CHEATSHEET.md) • [Architecture](./docs/architecture.md) • [Schema Specification](./docs/schema-spec.md) • [API Docs](./docs/api-reference.md) • [Roadmap](./ROADMAP.md) • [Changelog](./CHANGELOG.md)
---
## Why Jantt? The Declarative Revolution
Traditional project management and timeline tools force an impossible choice:
1. **Enterprise Bloat**: Commercial suites (DHTMLX, Bryntum) demand 200KB to 800KB runtime dependencies, complex imperative APIs (`gantt.init()`, `gantt.addTask()`), and expensive recurring per-seat fees.
2. **Brittle AI Generations**: Prompting LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) to generate React JSX or SVG coordinate math produces broken layouts, coordinate hallucinations, and wastes thousands of tokens on boilerplate UI code.
3. **Static Limitations**: DSLs like Mermaid.js are read-only, non-interactive images. They cannot be dragged, edited, recalculated, or synchronized back to living project state.

itens.readme:
Kubai Icons 
   An agent skill that draws animated icons in one consistent style.  
  Plus 2,800+ open-source icons drawn with it, for React, Vue and the web.
   Install the skill  ·
   Browse the icons  ·
   Use them in code  ·
   Docs 
## What's included
| Part | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| **Agent skill** | The rules, engine and self-check that draw every icon in one hand. Give Claude Code, Codex or another coding agent a product, and it draws the icons that product needs. |
| **Icon library** | 2,800+ icons: nearly 900 objects, plus badged and slashed "off" versions. For React, Vue, plain JavaScript, web components and static SVG. MIT licensed. |
| **Website** | [icons.kubai.design](https://icons.kubai.design/), in 16 languages. Search every icon by name, shape or meaning, recolor it, copy its code or a prompt for your agent, download it as SVG or PNG, and save a collection as a ZIP. |
## Install the skill
Copy this into your agent and send it:
```text
Install the Kubai Icons skill for me:
clone https://github.com/kubai087/kubai-icons into your skills folder as kubai-icons
(~/.claude/skills in Claude Code, ~/.agents/skills in Codex;
if it's already there, pull the latest version instead),
make sure SKILL.md exists in that folder, and tell me when it's ready.
```
Restart your agent, and the skill is ready. An agent without skill support can read `SKILL.md` from the cloned folder and follow it.
> [!TIP]
> The skill asks for careful geometry and several rounds of looking at its own screenshots, so use a capable model that can read images. It was developed and blind-tested with **Claude Opus 5.5**, which we recommend. Other models, such as GPT in Codex, can use the same skill. In Claude Code, run `claude --model claude-opus-5-5`.
  Install it yourself  
Clone the repository into your skills folder. In Codex, use `~/.agents/skills` instead.
```bash
git clone https://github.com/kubai087/kubai-icons.git ~/.claude/skills/kubai-icons
```
Or download `kubai-icons-v*.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/kubai087/kubai-icons/releases/latest) and unzip it there:
```bash
unzip kubai-icons-v*.zip -d ~/.claude/skills/
```
The agent picks the skill up the next time it starts.
Publishing to a skill marketplace that asks for a version and display names in `SKILL.md`? Upload `kubai-icons-v*-platform.zip` from the same release. It carries those fields at the top of the frontmatter.
